name: manifest
author: Astra <astrabrightwing@pm.me>
_comment_desktopName: Read by electron-builder, not by npm: it becomes the Linux .desktop filename and the window's WM_CLASS, which is what lets a desktop environment link the running window to its launcher icon.
_comment_naming: THE COMMENTS LIVE UP HERE, NOT IN "build". npm ignores unknown top-level keys; electron-builder SCHEMA-VALIDATES its own block and refuses to run on one it does not recognise, which is a failed release rather than a warning. Learned the hard way on 0.3.0-beta. The game is Manifest everywhere now — productName, build.productName, appId, the artifacts and the desktop entry — and the one thing that rename moves is where Electron keeps userData, which is derived from productName and is where the saves live. electron/main.js carries them across; see the note there before touching either name again.
_comment_maintainer: fpm refuses to build a .deb without a package maintainer, and what electron-builder looks for is `author` with an address in it. Astra's, given for the purpose. build.linux.maintainer repeats it rather than leaning on the fallback, so the .deb keeps naming a maintainer even if `author` is ever shortened back to a bare name. (It is a real electron-builder key, unlike a comment: see the note above about what that block does to anything it does not recognise.)
